rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing growth to earth is metaphorical and expansive: God is the actual one who makes plants grow.
rows.anchor: فهو مجاز لأن الأرض ينبت منها والله تعالى هو المنبت لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زوج means every kind of vegetation, including crops and planted growth; بهيج means pleasing, fresh, bright, and beautiful, as al-Mubarrad explains.
rows.anchor: والبهجة حسن الشيء ونضارته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The succession of contrary states in bodies is evidence for a maker; this establishes that God is the real, existent, and abiding one.
rows.anchor: حدوث هذه الأمراض المتنافية وتواردها على الأجسام يدل على وجود الصانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since bringing these things into being is not beyond God, bringing the dead back to life should not be considered impossible.
rows.anchor: لما لم يستبعد من الإله إيجاد هذه الأشياء فكيف يستبعد منه إعادة الأموات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who creates these things must be inherently characterized by power; whoever can do so can do every possible thing, including resurrection.
rows.anchor: ومن كان كذلك كان قادرا على جميع الممكنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection is possible, God can accomplish it, and the truthful report says it will occur; therefore its occurrence must be affirmed.
rows.anchor: الإعادة في نفسها ممكنة والصادق أخبر عن وقوعها فلا بد من القطع بوقوعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Separated bodies remain receptive to the properties they had while alive and rational: if their essential receptivity ever ceased, they could never have possessed life and reason.
rows.anchor: تلك الصفات لأنها لو لم تكن قابلة لها في وقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the specific parts of every morally responsible person and has power over all possibilities, so he can create those properties in those bodies.
rows.anchor: قادرا على إيجاد تلك الصفات في تلك الذوات

words: فَإِنَّا خَلَقْنَٰكُم مِّن تُرَابٍۢ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِن مُّضْغَةٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stages of animal and plant creation demonstrate God's knowledge of all facts and power over all possibilities, the two principles on which denial of resurrection depends.
rows.anchor: قادر على كل الممكنات وعالم بكل المعلومات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī links the first clause of 36:79 to divine power and its final clause to divine knowledge, the two premises for resurrection.
rows.anchor: بيان للقدرة وقوله : { وهو بكل خلق عليم }

none: Qur’an text only; no commentary in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has حق with ḍamma, while another reads حقا, making it an accusative emphasis that the punishment truly applies.
rows.anchor: قرى { حق } بالضم وقرىء حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مكرم is also read with fatḥa on rāʾ, with the sense of honoring or showing honor.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { مكرم } بفتح الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After saying that God guides whom he wills, the verse explains which groups he guides and which he does not.
rows.anchor: أتبعه في هذه الآية ببيان من يهديه ومن لا يهديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī classifies doctrinal disagreement into disputes among those sharing a prophet, disputes over prophethood, and disputes over God.
rows.anchor: أن المسلم لا يخالفه في المسائل الأصولية إلا طبقات ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first class shares a prophet but disputes issues such as human acts between Jabriyya and Qadariyya, and divine attributes and vision between their affirmers and deniers.
rows.anchor: الخلاف بين الجبرية والقدرية في خلق الأفعال البشرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second class accepts a free agent but disputes prophethood, as Muslims, Jews, and Christians dispute Muhammad, Jesus, and Moses.
rows.anchor: الذين يخالفونه في النبوة ولكن يشاركونه في الاعتراف بالفاعل المختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third class disputes God: sophists suspend judgment on realities, Dahriyya deny an agent, and philosophers posit a necessary rather than freely choosing agent; Rāzī calls this the greatest divide and says adherents conceal their views.
rows.anchor: أعظم جهات الخلاف هو من جهة القسم الأخير منها

words: وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ وَٱلصَّٰبِـِٔينَ وَٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوٓا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī's taxonomy names six religious communities: Muslims, Jews, Christians, Sabians, Magians who follow a false prophet, and prophet-denying idolaters including Brahmins.
rows.anchor: فهم المسلمون واليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
rows.claim: Qatāda and Muqātil say the religions are six: Islam belongs to God, and the other five belong to Satan.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة ومقاتل الأديان ستة واحدة لله تعالى

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ
rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says this clause is the predicate of the preceding إن الذين آمنوا; Jarīr's line is poetic evidence for that syntax.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج هذا خبر

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ
rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarīr's line إن الخليفة إن الله سربله is cited as poetic evidence for the clause functioning as a predicate after إن.
rows.anchor: قال جرير : إن الخليفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the separation is unrestricted, it may separate their circumstances and locations, varying their recompense and not gathering them in one place.
rows.anchor: الفصل مطلق فيحتمل الفصل بينهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation takes يفصل to mean that God judges among them.
rows.anchor: وقيل يفصل بينهم يقضي بينهم

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ شَهِيدٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's complete knowledge of each group's deserts ensures that his judgment contains no injustice or unfairness.
rows.anchor: عالم بما يستحقه كل منهم فلا يجري في ذلك الفصل ظلم ولا حيف

words: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here رؤية means knowing: people know this from God's report, not from having seen the prostration.
rows.anchor: أنها العلم أي ألم تعلم أن الله يسجد له

words: يَسْجُدُ لَهُۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj calls the best explanation of cosmic prostration obedient submission: created things accept God's acts without resistance, resembling obedience; he compares this with verses on creation's submission and praise.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج أجود الوجوه في سجود هذه الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although all are naturally subject to God, rebellious people refuse prostration outwardly; believers submit both inherently and outwardly, explaining why only many people are singled out.
rows.anchor: بعضهم تمرد وتكبر وترك السجود في الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing detaches this phrase: the first prostration means submission, the second worship; another makes كثير من الناس a subject with omitted predicate ‘rewarded’; a third repeats كثير to magnify the number deserving punishment.
rows.anchor: قامت الدلالة على أنه لا يجوز استعمال اللفظ المشترك في معنييه جميعا

words: يَسْجُدُ لَهُۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who allow a homonym to carry two senses take rational beings' prostration as worship and inanimates' as submission; opponents say the word is used twice with these respective senses.
rows.anchor: من يجوز استعمال اللفظ المشترك في مفهوميه جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general wording in 13:15 includes people, but mentioning many people separately prevents the mistaken inference that all humans prostrate as all angels do.
rows.anchor: لو اقتصر على ما تقدم لأوهم أن كل الناس يسجدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under that reading, those who refuse prostration are the many people for whom punishment is due.
rows.anchor: وهم الذين حق عليهم العذاب

words: يَسْجُدُ لَهُۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that every contingent being depends on the Necessary Being for existence at its beginning and continuation; this intrinsic need is deeper humility than the physical gesture of prostration.
rows.anchor: كل ما سوى الله تعالى فهو ممكن لذاته

words: يَسْجُدُ لَهُۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl applies this dependence to the verse: contingent things are humbled before God and confess need for his bringing them into existence, linking it with 17:44.
rows.anchor: فجميع الممكنات ساجدة بهذا المعنى لله تعالى

words: يَسْجُدُ لَهُۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid's third explanation is that things prostrate through their shadows, as in the verse about shadows inclining in prostration.
rows.anchor: أن سجود هذه الأشياء سجود ظلها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report through ʿAṭāʾ, Ibn ʿAbbās says many people affirm God's oneness, while those due punishment do not.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء وكثير من الناس يوحده

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās says many people are in Paradise, supporting the analysis that كثير من الناس is a subject with an omitted predicate.
rows.anchor: وروى عنه أيضا أنه قال وكثير من الناس في الجنة

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others pause after كثير من الناس and start a new sentence: many others deserve punishment because they refuse and abstain from prostrating.
rows.anchor: قال آخرون : الوقف على قوله

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدَٰفِعُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explaining pilgrimage rites and benefits, Rāzī notes that unbelievers had blocked pilgrimage; the passage now explains removing that obstacle and securing access to pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: لما بين ما يلزم الحج ومناسكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, and Nāfiʿ read يدافع with alif and similarly دفع next; Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr omit alif in both; Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and ʿĀṣim use it here but omit it in دفع.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع بالألف

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: With the alif, يدافع conveys intensive defense; al-Khalīl says دفعا is the verbal noun of دفع and دفاعا of دافع, with دفاع the better form.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ يدافع فمعناه يبالغ في الدفع عنهم

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدَٰفِعُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of God's defense is unstated, making the expression grander and more general, though in reality he defends against the polytheists' force.
rows.anchor: لم يذكر ما يدفعه حتى يكون أفخم وأعظم وأعم

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ خَوَّانٍ كَفُورٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following clause identifies the kind of people whose schemes God repels from believers: treacherous and ungrateful unbelievers.
rows.anchor: يدفع عن المؤمنين كيد من هذا صفته

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدَٰفِعُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟
rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says God protected believers in Mecca from its unbelievers before the Hijra, when persecuted Muslims asked the Prophet to let them kill tormentors secretly and he forbade it.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : إن الله يدافع كفار مكة

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدَٰفِعُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse promises believers victory over unbelievers and protection from their violence, paralleling promises in 3:111, 40:51, 37:172, and 61:13.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية بشارة للمؤمنين بإعلائهم على الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خَوَّان betrays God's trust and كَفُور is ungrateful for his blessing; Rāzī links this to 8:27.
rows.anchor: الخوان الكفور أي خوان في أمانة الله كفور

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says they acknowledged the Creator but worshipped another, which he calls the greatest betrayal.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل أقروا بالصانع وعبدوا غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Medina and Basra and ʿĀṣim in Ḥafṣ's transmission read أذن with ḍamma on hamza; the rest read it with fatḥa, meaning God gave permission to fight.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة والبصرة وعاصم في رواية حفص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Medina and ʿĀṣim read يقاتلون with fatḥa on tāʾ; Ibn Kathīr, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read the specified variant with kasra on tāʾ and a different form of أذن.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة وعاصم { يقاتلون } بنصب التاء

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj explain one reading as permission for those keen to fight polytheists in the future; with active يقاتلون, it means permission to fight.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء والزجاج : يعني أذن الله للذين يحرصون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction omits the object of permission; it means permission to fight, supplied by the following يقاتلون.
rows.anchor: في الآية محذوف والتقدير أذن للذين يقاتلون في القتال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccan polytheists severely abused the companions; beaten and wounded Muslims complained to the Prophet, who told them to be patient until after the Hijra, when this first fighting permission came after more than seventy prohibitions.
rows.anchor: وهم أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان مشركوا مكة يؤذونهم أذى شديدا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says the verse concerned migrants intercepted by Meccan polytheists, after which they were permitted to fight.
rows.anchor: وقيل نزلت في قوم خرجوا مهاجرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This promises that God will aid them: saying one is able to reward an obedient person can idiomatically mean that one will do so, not merely that one has ability.
rows.anchor: فذلك وعد منه تعالى بنصرهم

words: ٱلَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا۟ مِن دِيَٰرِهِم بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their oppression had two parts: they were expelled from their homes and expelled for saying God is their Lord; each is a grave injustice.
rows.anchor: فبين تعالى ظلمهم لهم بهذين الوجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception means they were expelled with no cause other than affirming God's oneness, which should warrant acceptance and protection, not expulsion and banishment.
rows.anchor: التوحيد الذي ينبغي أن يكون موجب الإقرار والتمكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī compares the wording with 5:59, where believers are challenged for nothing except that they believed in God.
rows.anchor: ومثله { هل تنقمون منا إلا أن ءامنا بالله }

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's established practice is to preserve his religion by having some people repel others.
rows.anchor: أن عادته جل جلاله أن يحفظ دينه بهذا الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads لهدمت with a light consonant; the other readers use the doubled consonant.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع { لهدمت } بالتخفيف

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī explains defense as God permitting his people to fight unbelievers; otherwise polytheists would dominate religious communities and destroy worship places, while the command lets believers worship and build.
rows.anchor: هو إذنه لأهل دينه بمجاهدة الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Non-Muslim worship sites are included because the defense preserves places of worship for communities beyond the Muslims.
rows.anchor: ولكنه دفع عن هؤلاء بأن أمر بقتال أعداء الدين

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ
rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says God protects believers through prophets and protects those who do not fight through those who fight.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي يدفع الله بالنبيين عن المؤمنين

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abū al-Jawzāʾ reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that good-doers protect wrongdoers, and those who pray, give alms, and perform pilgrimage protect those who do not.
rows.anchor: روى أبو الجوزاء عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet said God protects a hundred members of a righteous Muslim's household and neighbors through him, then recited this verse; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ
rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports Ibn ʿAbbās's view that Islam and its adherents protect the protected non-Muslim communities.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says witnesses protect people's rights and legal retaliation protects lives.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد يدفع عن الحقوق بالشهود

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes all these terms to mean places of worship used by believers, with different expressions for them.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن المراد بهذه المواضع أجمع مواضع المؤمنين

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says each prophet's lawful prayer place was protected in its era: churches under Moses, monasteries under Jesus, and mosques under Muhammad, before distortion and abrogation.
rows.anchor: فلولا ذلك الدفع لهدم في زمن موسى الكنائس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation includes the sites because God's name continued to be remembered in them in the Prophet's time, so they were unlike idol worship.
rows.anchor: يجري فيها ذكر الله تعالى فليست بمنزلة عبادة الأوثان

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya assigns monasteries to Christians, churches to Jews, prayer houses to Sabians, and mosques to Muslims.
rows.anchor: الصوامع للنصارى والبيع لليهود

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says monasteries are Christian desert buildings, churches Christian buildings in towns, and prayer houses belong to Jews; ṣalawāt is Hebrew ṣəlōṯā.
rows.anchor: الصوامع للنصارى وهي التي بنوها في الصحارى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda assigns monasteries to Sabians, churches to Christians, and prayer houses to Jews.
rows.anchor: الصوامع للصابئين والبيع للنصارى والصلوات لليهود عن قتادة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says all four terms denote mosques: Muslims may use monasteries, churches is a comparison for mosques, and prayer houses refers to prayer and mosques being preserved.
rows.anchor: أنها بأسرها أسماء المساجد عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One figurative explanation of destroying prayers is invalidating them and eliminating their performers, as when someone's kindness is destroyed by answering it with ingratitude.
rows.anchor: المراد بهدم الصلاة إبطالها وإهلاك من يفعلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes صلوات as the place of prayer, as 'ask the town' means ask its people.
rows.anchor: بل المراد مكان الصلوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view allows an item that cannot be destroyed to join a list whose other items can, like saying someone carries a sword and a spear.
rows.anchor: كقولهم متقلدا سيفا ورمحا

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil take the frequent remembrance of God's name to refer to all the listed worship places.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل عائد إلى الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says the phrase more likely refers only to mosques, honoring them as places where God is frequently remembered.
rows.anchor: والأقرب أنه مختص بالمساجد تشريفا لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other worship sites precede mosques because they existed earlier; another explanation says the last-mentioned were last historically, though first in intention, since Muhammad and his community were best and last, as in the Prophet's saying, 'we are the last and the foremost'.
rows.anchor: لأنها أقدم في الوجود

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view says aiding God means accepting jihad and thereby supporting God's religion.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم من ينصره بتلقى الجهاد بالقبول

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another view understands aiding God as upholding all his religion; God cannot literally be aided, so the expression means aiding his religion, as with being God's ally or enemy.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل المراد من يقوم بسائر دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise aids those who support God's religion: he strengthens them against enemies until they prevail, helps them explain proofs, and assists them in knowledge and obedience, encouraging jihad.
rows.anchor: وعد بالنصر لمن هذه حاله ونصر الله تعالى للعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's strength assures his promised aid; his might means he cannot be wronged or prevented from what he wills.
rows.anchor: قوي على هذه النصرة التي وعدها المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Empowerment on earth means sovereignty and effective rule over people, not mere basic ability, which all people have and which would not entail the ensuing duties.
rows.anchor: المراد من هذا التمكن السلطنة ونفاذ القول على الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people empowered are the Muhājirūn: 22:41 describes those expelled from their homes, while the Anṣār were not expelled.
rows.anchor: والأنصار ما أخرجوا من ديارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says the Muhājirūn would perform four duties when empowered: establish prayer, give alms, command right, and forbid wrong.
rows.anchor: فإنهم أتوا بالأمور الأربعة ، وهي إقامة الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the four caliphs were empowered rulers and performed these duties, and commanded all right and prohibited all wrong, Rāzī argues they were rightly guided and the verse proves their imamate.
rows.anchor: قد ثبت أن الله تعالى مكن الأئمة الأربعة من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects reading the verse as referring to ʿAlī alone because its wording denotes a group.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز حمل الآية على علي عليه السلام وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final outcome belongs to God: the promised sovereignty will certainly occur, and all affairs return to his enduring rule.
rows.anchor: لا يزول ملكه أبدا وهو أيضا يؤكد ما قلناه

none: Qur’an text only; no commentary in this segment.
